chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Dawud al-Mustarriq, from Sufyan ibn Mus'ab al-Abdi, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he said: 'Tell Umm Farwa to come and listen to what was done with her grandfather.' He said: So she came and sat behind the curtain. Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Recite a poem to us.' I said: 'Let Farwa be generous with your flowing tears.' He said: So she wailed and the women wailed. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The door! The door!' So the people of Medina gathered at the door. He said: So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) sent a message to them: 'A young one of ours fainted, hence the women wailed.'

key_terms.أُمِّ فَرْوَةَ: Umm Farwa, a relative of the Prophet
key_terms.جَدِّهَا: Her grandfather (referring to the Prophet Muhammad)
key_terms.فَرْوُ جُودِي: Let Farwa be generous (a poetic invocation)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) convey the grief for the Prophet to the people of Medina?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Imam's strategic use of auditory signals to convey the depth of Ahl al-Bayt's grief to the public during a period of political tension. By employing a boy in a trance-like state to mimic the women's wailing, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) demonstrated a nuanced method of distinguishing genuine mourning from mere noise, thereby preserving the sanctity of their sorrow. This incident underscores the scholarly view that the Ahl al-Bayt actively engaged in public commemoration of the Prophet's legacy, using cultural norms of lamentation to assert their emotional and spiritual connection to the Prophet.
